title: Threats of Political Violence Have America’s Elected Officials Living in Fear
partialText: A Times investigation has found that violent threats have become a new normal among public officials, reshaped private lives, cost millions in security and pushed people out of office.

title: After Many Threats, an Arizona Lawmaker Asks: ‘Is It Really Worth It?’
partialText: Threats have altered the lives of State Representative Alma Hernandez, her family, friends and neighbors. They have even transformed her policymaking.

title: Saudi and Yemeni Airports Hit in New Round of Strikes
partialText: The airport in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, was struck a day after suffering a devastating attack. The Houthis said Saudi aircraft hit the Yemeni capital’s airport.

title: Saudi Arabia Has Few Options as Houthis Aim at Heart of Its Ambitions
partialText: Three deadly attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen on an airport in the Saudi capital underscored the asymmetrical nature of their conflict with the kingdom.

title: Ukraine Shrugs Off Trump Call to Ditch Zelensky for Energy Strikes
partialText: President Trump lashed out at President Volodymyr Zelensky for striking Russian oil refineries. Mr. Zelensky said he’ll stop — if Russia does too.

title: A Russian Spy’s Lone Regret: ‘I Got Caught’
partialText: Though born in Ukraine, Alexsander supports the Russian cause. He wishes he had deleted one photo from his phone.

title: In Unlikely Turn, Law and Order Heats Up L.A. Mayor’s Race
partialText: Two Democratic candidates choose opposite tacks on public safety and policing, seeking to corral undecided voters.

title: A Reporter Returns to China to Find it Richer, but Also Highly Paranoid.
partialText: Returning to China after decades away, a correspondent finds bullet trains, dazzling skylines — and a surveillance state more paranoid and pervasive than ever.

title: How the White House Manufactured a Narrative About a Trump Aide’s Call Logs
partialText: A release of selected records from the classified documents inquiry is a case study in how omitting context can create political ammunition.

title: Democrats Press Pentagon on Iran Civilian Deaths
partialText: A new letter from 74 lawmakers suggests that civilian casualties will become a focus of investigation if Democrats take control of Congress.

title: Four Hours and Three Minutes in Ithaca
partialText: On the most traumatic night in a young woman’s life, a good man could not be found.

title: Samuel Alito and New Jersey’s Fallen Columbus Statue
partialText: Justice Alito has a history of nudging the boundaries of judicial rectitude.

title: India’s Youth Protests Challenge Narendra Modi
partialText: Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India has long succeeded in isolating and undermining opponents. The Gen Z protests pose a challenge unlike any he has faced before.
